office.title: WordCraft
office.text: A word processor for longer documents, everyday writing and page layout. The Haiku port keeps the Rust editor and adds native desktop integration.
features: DOCX documents, styled text, tables, page layout and PDF export
Review tools and document recovery
Native Open/Save panels, clipboard and sharp text on scaled displays

office.title: GridCraft
office.text: A spreadsheet for budgets, calculations and charts, with a familiar ribbon and formula bar.
features: XLSX workbooks, formulas, number formats and charts
Native file panels and text/HTML clipboard integration
Tracker document handling and display-density support

office.title: DeckCraft
office.text: Build a presentation, add speaker notes and take it fullscreen on your Haiku desktop.
features: PPTX and DeckCraft documents, PDF and image export
Transitions, animations and a native fullscreen slide show
Media Kit audio, native file panels and recovery for unsaved work

office.title: PDFCraft
office.text: Read and work on PDFs in a native window, with the same Rust document engine used on the other platforms.
features: Search and copy text, annotate, edit and organize pages
Fill forms, save changes and undo edits
Native file panels, document recovery and an included command-line tool

media.title: Media preferences
media.text: Audio and video settings have been rebuilt around a sidebar and readable cards, so devices and everyday controls are easier to find.
features: Choose input and output devices, adjust volume and play a test sound
Control individual applications in the audio mixer, with app icons and mute controls
Check a live recording level meter and camera preview
Choose a MIDI SoundFont and restart stopped media services

media.title: MediaConverter
media.text: A new conversion window and engine bring queues, previews and hardware-aware encoding to Haiku’s media toolbox.
features: Queue video and audio files, preview sources and choose separate video or audio presets
Audio conversion keeps artwork, tags and chapters, with playback controls in the source preview
Use available GPU encoders, inspect video hardware and see when a job will use the CPU
Import DVD/Blu-ray sources and disc images, sidecar subtitles and embedded closed captions
Preserve HDR10 metadata where supported; conversions run in worker processes and retry on the CPU after a GPU crash
Use the mediaconvert command-line tool for scripted conversions
